sampling_model.design: Observational covariance-fiber analysis with no interventions; the population complexity problem receives exact rational \(\Sigma\).
sampling_model.units: For the inference rung, \(X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(n)}\) are independent centered Gaussian vectors in \(\mathbb R^p\).
sampling_model.treatment: No designated treatment is needed for orientation recovery; optional vertices \(x\) and \(y\) index a total-effect projection.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The population kernel uses exact Schur complements. The inference rung uses a simultaneous covariance region and performs no direct equality test on \(\widehat\Sigma\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The directed acyclic graph can be recovered from the joint Gaussian distribution under equal error variances.
Sources are identified by the smallest marginal variance, followed by conditional-variance source removal.
The variables are partitioned into blocks and each block shares the same error variance.
A generic distribution in a vertex-colored Gaussian DAG model is faithful to its DAG.
The minimum-label problems considered are W[2]-hard in the number of used labels.
Binary CSP on graph classes of unbounded treewidth has an ETH lower bound with a treewidth-over-log-treewidth exponent.
Set Cover has a base-two incidence-pathwidth barrier under the primal-pathwidth SETH.
An ASP reduction induces a polynomial-time bijection between the solution sets of the two instances.
An FPT-computable neighborhood function yields ordered Delay-FPT enumeration through a priority queue.
Split likelihood-ratio inversion gives finite-sample-valid total-effect confidence regions under equal variances.
Residual goodness-of-fit tests are inverted to construct confidence sets for causal orderings.

body.tldr: Arbitrary Gaussian error variances identify only a Markov-equivalence class, one common variance identifies the DAG, and a supplied partial-homoscedastic partition refines the class. This project studies the missing observational regime in which the equality partition is not supplied: a faithful rational Gaussian forest covariance is compatible with a root tuple when its exact regression residuals use at most \(K\) numerical values. The proved rational-tree-realization theorem fixes the diagonal separately from the off-diagonal path products and establishes the arbitrary-root SEM covariance identity, both directed edge residuals, positive definiteness, faithfulness, rationality, and polynomial bit length. It proves the exact supplied-order dynamic program and the bounded-component \(d^K\) algorithm, while posing the unrestricted FPT-versus-parameterized-hard classification in \(K\), the unrestricted uniqueness classification, and the matching recurrence-width lower bound as explicit open questions; two-witness recovery is proved in the two algorithmic regimes and has a one-way feasibility transfer. A covariance-region projection then propagates sampling uncertainty to orientations and total effects.

project_justification.gap: Published equal-variance and partial-homoscedastic theory either fixes one common level or supplies the equality partition. Generic minimum-label hardness does not survive the algebraic and arithmetic restrictions of Gaussian residual signatures.
project_justification.niche: The exact latent-\(K\) covariance fiber is a pointwise structural-identification object lying between fully identified equal-error models and unrestricted Markov equivalence, with a parameter whose algorithmic status is unknown.
project_justification.fill: The project gives a root-union reduction, an exact rational tree-signature realization theorem with the piecewise diagonal and path-product covariance reconstructed by an arbitrary-root SEM, symbolic root loci, positive algorithms at bounded component size and bounded recurrence width, and an answer-open classification theorem whose negative branch must certify edge residuals, positive definiteness, faithfulness, rationality, and bit length before using any Gaussian gadget.

body.related_work: Peters and Buehlmann (2014) establish full identification when all innovation variances are equal, the \(K=1\) endpoint. Chen, Drton, and Wang (2019) exploit the same common-variance ordering to build scalable recovery algorithms. Wu and Drton (2023) characterize Gaussian DAG equivalence when the variance partition is supplied and therefore motivate the latent-partition step without occupying it. Boege, Kubjas, Misra, and Solus (2026) provide rational parameter recovery, algebraic Markov descriptions, and generic faithfulness for fixed vertex colorings; the inverse theorem here instead couples every alternative root of one covariance and certifies its piecewise diagonal and off-diagonal tree-product matrix by an arbitrary-root SEM calculation, including both directed edge residuals and polynomial bit length. Fellows, Guo, and Kanj (2010) show that several unrestricted minimum-label graph problems are W[2]-hard, but their label systems are not Gaussian-realizable. Marx (2010) and Lampis (2025) supply decomposition and fine-grained lower-bound techniques for CSP and Set Cover interfaces. Yato and Seta (2003) and Creignou et al. (2013) show why another-solution recovery needs solution-preserving reductions and a canonical neighborhood. Strieder and Drton (2023) and Wang, Kolar, and Drton (2026) motivate projecting structural uncertainty to total effects; the projection proposition here is deliberately supporting rather than advertised as a new optimal inference theorem.
body.technical_internal_limitation: A common-center star encoding of Set Cover has a universal two-label center-root witness, while varying centers creates complementary residual labels. Moreover, every edge satisfies \(a_u b_{v\mid u}=a_v b_{u\mid v}\), and rational covariance requires a rational-square edge reconstruction. The first reduction test therefore enumerates one three-choice selector and one compatibility component, including all internal roots; any unintended witness or nonconstant auxiliary-label charge rejects that template. The existing twin-star family also rules out raw representative compression at empty width-one cuts, but it does not rule out a different symbolic FPT algorithm.
body.honest_scope: The root-union, root-locus, bounded-choice, ordered-DP, piecewise rational-tree-realization, two-witness-transfer, \(K=1\), and projection-coverage results are proved in this note. In particular, `thm:rational-tree-realization` proves the arbitrary-root SEM covariance identity, both directed residual identities, positive definiteness, tree faithfulness, rationality, and polynomial bit length, and includes a three-vertex nonunit-diagonal check. These theorem-level facts are available as certificates, but every proposed hardness or lower-bound gadget must still verify the realization theorem's hypotheses and enumerate every unintended root and auxiliary label. The headline \(K\)-classification, the arbitrary-algorithm \(q_\pi\) lower bound, and the uniqueness transfer remain open-ended questions. The proposition at \(K=1\) is the required reduction to PetersBuhlmann2014. The confidence projection claims coverage but not efficient optimization, likelihood-ratio calibration, unknown-mean adjustment, or robustness to approximate equality.
